header: The first three months on Larkmoor Depot
lead: Each company below runs Larkmoor Depot as its only stock system. We asked each one for a sentence and printed it unchanged.

quotes.quote_text: The counter can now promise a delivery date without walking to the back. That walk used to happen many times a day.
quotes.author: Katrin Weissgruber

image.alternative: Portrait of a man in his forties.

quotes.quote_text: Stocktaking used to close us for a Saturday. Last year we counted two aisles a week on a handheld and never closed at all.
quotes.author: Milan Prohaska

image.alternative: Portrait of a woman in her sixties.

quotes.quote_text: I order based on what we actually sold, not on what I remember selling. The reorder list was wrong twice this year, and both times it was my mistake.
quotes.author: Doris Ebner

image.alternative: Portrait of a man in his thirties.

quotes.quote_text: Each of our parts has four names, depending on who is asking. We can keep all four and search by any of them.
quotes.author: Stefan Aigner

image.alternative: Portrait of a woman in her twenties.

quotes.quote_text: Two of us run this shop. I didn't want a system that assumes a purchasing department, and this one never asked if we had one.
quotes.author: Lena Brandtner

image.alternative: Portrait of a man in his fifties.

quotes.quote_text: Dispatch prints the delivery note, the customer signs on screen, and the invoice goes out the same evening. Nobody retypes anything.
quotes.author: Tobias Reisinger

image.alternative: Portrait of a woman in her fifties.
